Maintenance Report — MNT-0199-009

Asset: WELL-0199 (NE-08 Well 199, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 05 Apr 2024 08:00 · Finished: 05 Apr 2024 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0199-0076 on 2024-04-04 Report written: 06 Apr 2024

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0199-0076 at 07:30 on 2024-04-04 found crude oil on the pad: about 5.4% of the pad area, estimated 2.5 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.1 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 212 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 170 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 1.9 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0199-009 (WS-06).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0199-020

Asset: WELL-0199 (NE-08 Well 199, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 15 Jun 2025 08:00 · Finished: 25 Jun 2025 21:00 · Well stopped for this job: 253 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0199-0137 on 2025-06-12 Report written: 25 Jun 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0199-0137 showed the wellhead at 32.4 °C with the air at 31.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 9 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0199-031

Asset: WELL-0199 (NE-08 Well 199, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 26 Sep 2026 08:00 · Finished: 06 Oct 2026 12:00 · Well stopped for this job: 244 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0199-0202 on 2026-09-24 Report written: 06 Oct 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the wellhead was cold and the pump jack was straining with a heavy, uneven load. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0199-0202 showed the wellhead at 23.9 °C with the air at 24.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 8 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A worn plunger that let sand settle and lock the pump.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.
